A device that transmits and modifies force, motion, or energy to perform a specific task. Parameters: energy input (power source and form), mechanical advantage (force/motion amplification ratio), component count and topology (how parts link to transmit force), transmission mechanism (gears, linkages, belts, screws, cams that convert motion types). Persistence mechanism: mechanical engineering practice — codified through ISO, ASME, and DIN standards for machine elements; taught through formal engineering curricula and industrial apprenticeship; preserved in technical documentation, patents, and machine shops.

An actuator is an engineered component that converts one form of energy into controlled mechanical motion. Parameters: energy source (electrical current, compressed gas, hydraulic pressure, or thermal expansion), motion output (linear stroke, rotary rotation, or oscillatory swing), and control interface (analog signal, digital command, or manual input). The actuator's role is to translate abstract control signals into physical force and displacement within a mechanism, serving as the effector in a closed control loop. Persistence: physical fabrication from engineered materials (metals, polymers, composites), assembled from precision-machined parts, maintained through scheduled replacement. [formal: actuarius | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A spring is a mechanical element designed to deform under applied force and recover its original shape when the force is removed, thereby storing and releasing mechanical energy. It is manufactured from elastic materials (most commonly steel alloys, but also polymers, ceramics, and composites) into specific geometries — helical, leaf, torsion, gas, or fluid — each optimized for a particular mode of deformation (compression, extension, torsion, or bending). The persistence mechanism is the material's elastic modulus: when stressed within the elastic limit, atomic bonds stretch elastically, storing potential energy that is returned as mechanical work upon unloading. [formal: springum | substrate: matter | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A whistle is a human-made acoustic device that produces a clear, sustained tone when air is forced through an opening. It consists of a chamber or tube with a mouthpiece, a windway that directs airflow against a sharp edge (the fipple), and an escape hole that creates the oscillation. The pitch is determined by the chamber size and any openings (finger holes, valves) that change the effective air column length. Whistles are built from materials including metal, plastic, wood, or ceramic, and persist through manufacture, use, and transmission across generations as a simple, reliable means of producing standardized sounds for signaling, sport, music, or warning. [formal: whistle | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A chant is a vocal practice in which speech-like text is repeated at a steady, often musical, pitch — situated between ordinary speech and full singing. Its parameters are: (1) a textual body that is typically rhythmic and formulaic (mantra, prayer, work-cry, incantation, or call-and-response refrain); (2) a narrow pitch range with limited melodic contour, where rhythmic recitation dominates over pitch variation; (3) a repetitive structure designed for endurance — enabling groups to sustain the same utterance in unison or turn-taking over extended periods. The persistence mechanism is oral tradition and group practice: chants survive through collective repetition in ritual, labor, pedagogy, and ceremony, where the act of chanting together reinforces both the text and the social bond. [formal: cantus | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A tangent is a straight line that touches a curve at exactly one point while sharing the curve's instantaneous slope at that point. Its parameters are: (1) a base curve defined by a differentiable function, (2) a point of tangency on the curve, (3) the derivative of the function at that point, which gives the line's slope. It persists through formal mathematical proof, analytical computation via differentiation, and geometric visualization in the Cartesian plane. [formal: tangens | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A lullaby is a song sung or played to soothe a child into sleep. Its parameters are: (1) a simple melodic contour with narrow pitch range and repetitive phrasing; (2) a tempo matching or slowing toward resting heart rate; (3) an address directed at or near a sleeping or drowsy child. It persists through oral transmission and written notation across generations — each performance renews the form, while the shared features (lulling purpose, simplified melody, repetitive structure) mark it as the same construct. [formal: lullaby | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Attunement is the act or process of adjusting oneself—or an object one controls—to align with a target standard, frequency, rhythm, or disposition. Its parameters are: (1) a target to align with (a pitch, a person's mood, a cultural norm, a mechanical baseline); (2) an adjustment mechanism (tuning pegs, behavioral modification, attentive listening, iterative calibration); (3) a feedback signal indicating proximity to alignment. It persists through repeated performance and the shared vocabulary of alignment—words like 'tune,' 'sync,' 'resonate,' and 'match' all point to this same constructed practice. [formal: attunement | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A heuristic-method is a human-created problem-solving technique that substitutes practical shortcuts, rules of thumb, or experience-based approximations for exhaustive algorithmic procedures. Its parameters are: (1) a goal state that need not be globally optimal, only satisfactorily reached; (2) a constraint (time, information, or computational) that makes exhaustive search infeasible; (3) a domain-specific insight that biases the search toward promising solutions. It persists through transmission (teaching, documentation, oral tradition) and through repeated deployment in practice, where effective heuristics survive as shared technique. [formal: methodus empirica | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A digression is a rhetorical device in which a speaker or writer temporarily departs from the main subject of discourse to explore a related but non-essential idea, then returns to the original topic. Its parameters are: (1) a main topic or argument being pursued; (2) a departure point where the discourse shifts to a tangentially related subject; (3) a return point where the discourse reconnects to the main thread. It persists through the teaching of rhetorical techniques, analysis of narrative structure in literature and rhetoric, and the study of how human attention is directed and redirected in communication. [formal: digressio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.99]

A codpiece is a separate garment piece attached to the front of breeches or trunk hose that covers and accentuates the male genital area. Its parameters are: (1) a distinct panel of fabric or leather, (2) attached to lower-body garments at the crotch seam, (3) shaped to provide coverage and often decorative emphasis. It persists through fashion tradition, theatrical costume practice, and historical reenactment — documented in clothing archives, fashion history texts, and museum collections. [formal: verutum | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

Mediation is a structured dispute resolution process in which a neutral third party — the mediator — facilitates communication and negotiation between disputing parties without imposing a binding decision. Its parameters are: (1) voluntary participation by all parties, (2) a neutral facilitator who has no authority to impose outcomes, (3) confidential proceedings, and (4) focus on interests rather than positions. It persists through institutional adoption in legal and organizational systems, professional mediator training programs, and sustained practice that maintains the role and technique across disputes. [formal: mediatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A promise is a speech act by which a speaker undertakes an obligation to bring about a future action or state of affairs. Its parameters are: (1) a speaker who declares commitment, (2) a hearer to whom the commitment is directed, (3) a specific content describing what will be done or ensured, and (4) the creation of a normative expectation enforceable by social sanction. It persists through interpersonal memory, social practice, and the reputational consequences of fulfillment or breach. [formal: promissio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A bell is a hollow resonator — typically a cast-metal cup or chamber — designed to produce a sustained, characteristic tone when its exterior is struck. Its parameters are: (1) a resonant body (metal, ceramic, wood, or other rigid material) shaped to amplify sound at a preferred frequency, (2) a striker (internal clapper, external mallet, or the bell itself swung against a fixed frame), and (3) a mounting system that allows the body to vibrate freely. The bell persists through casting or fabrication practice passed across generations, and through its embedded role in cultural traditions — from temple and church towers to maritime signals and timekeeping. [formal: campana | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An envelope is a foldable enclosure made of thin sheet material (paper, parchment, or synthetic polymer) whose parameters are: (1) a single sheet folded and sealed along edges to form a pocket, (2) a closure mechanism (glued flap, self-seal adhesive, or tie) that maintains enclosure integrity during handling, (3) a flat exterior surface for addressing, and (4) an interior void for containing documents, cards, or lightweight objects. The persistence mechanism is institutional standardization: postal authorities and commercial vendors enforce size, material, and sealing specifications that ensure compatibility with automated sorting and manual handling systems. The envelope endures because the cost of replacing it — redesigning global mail logistics, retraining workers, retooling factories — far exceeds the cost of maintaining a simple folded sheet.\n\n[formal: bulla | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A gazetteer is a systematically compiled reference work that catalogs geographical place names alongside structured descriptive information. Its parameters are: (1) a compiled list of named places drawn from survey, record, or field observation, (2) for each place, structured metadata including location coordinates or relative position and at least one descriptive attribute (topography, population, landmarks, or administrative status), (3) an organizational scheme enabling systematic retrieval — alphabetical by name, geographical by region, or hierarchical by political division. It persists as a published reference work maintained through periodic revision. [formal: geographicum | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An anvil is a heavy metal block — typically of cast iron, forged steel, or steel-on-iron composite — with a flat working face, a horn for shaping curves, and a bick for finer work. It provides a rigid, resilient surface that absorbs hammer blows while reflecting force back into the workpiece. The anvil persists through physical durability and through craft tradition: each new smith inherits standardized forms, dimensions, and techniques from prior generations, maintaining the tool's operational knowledge across generations of metalworking. [formal: incud | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A soundboard (also called a top or belly) is a flat, resonant wooden panel built into the body of acoustic stringed instruments — guitars, violins, cellos, and similar lutes — that receives mechanical vibrations from the strings via a bridge and amplifies them by coupling the string vibrations to the surrounding air. It is carved from tonewood chosen for its stiffness-to-weight ratio and internal damping properties, and its thickness, bracing pattern, and crown are tuned to produce a desired timbre and volume. [formal: soundboardum | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.12]

A clamp is a holding device composed of two parallel jaws and a force-generating mechanism that draws them together to secure objects in place. The mechanism varies by type — a screw clamp uses threaded rotation, a spring clamp uses elastic tension, a toggle clamp uses mechanical advantage, and a C-clamp combines a C-shaped frame with a lead screw. The jaws may be flat, curved, or padded depending on the application. Clamps persist as physical artifacts shaped by manufacturing processes (casting, machining, molding) and their form is maintained through material integrity. [formal: clampa | substrate: matter | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.12]

A humming is a vocal technique in which a person produces a steady tonal sound by vibrating the vocal folds while the lips remain closed and the mouth cavity forms a resonating chamber. The technique requires breath control, pitch awareness, and the ability to sustain a single frequency. It persists through the body's vocal apparatus and is transmitted via air as an audible waveform. Humming serves multiple purposes: self-regulation (calming the nervous system through vagal stimulation), musical practice (vocal warm-up, overtone exploration), and non-verbal communication (expressing contentment or absence). [formal: susurrus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A kiln is a thermally insulated chamber designed to reach and maintain elevated temperatures for the purpose of firing ceramics, sintering powders, or calcining materials. Its parameters are: (1) a combustion chamber or heating element that generates controlled heat; (2) refractory lining that retains thermal energy; (3) a means of temperature regulation (damper, vent, or electronic control); and (4) a load chamber where the workpiece sits. The persistence mechanism is physical construction — built from fired clay, brick, or stone, and sustained by fuel (wood, gas, electricity). Once built, a kiln persists as a durable artifact until destroyed. [formal: clibnum | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Resonance is the concept by which humans categorize the phenomenon of amplified response when a driving frequency matches or approaches a system's natural frequency. Its parameters: (1) a driven system with natural frequencies (normal modes), (2) a periodic driving force at or near those frequencies, (3) energy transfer from driver to system resulting in amplitude growth, (4) a quality factor (Q) that measures the sharpness and magnitude of amplification. The resonance concept persists through mathematical formalism (differential equations of driven oscillators), practical application (instrument design, structural engineering, radio tuning), and metaphorical extension (social resonance, empathic resonance). It is a map of a physical phenomenon, not the phenomenon itself — the concept exists independently in physics, chemistry, psychology, and sociology. [formal: resonantia | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A human-made concept for a character virtue in which a person maintains a modest assessment of their own importance, abilities, and fallibility — not self-erasure, but the disciplined correction of self-inflation. It operates as a social regulator (modesty norms), a spiritual discipline (humility before the divine), and an intellectual stance (awareness of cognitive limits). [formal: humilitas | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A human-made concept describing the state of strain produced when incompatible or mutually inconsistent elements co-occur — whether acoustic frequencies that resist harmonic combination, beliefs that contradict one another, or any system containing elements that cannot be simultaneously resolved. The concept carves three parameters: (1) the presence of two or more elements, (2) their mutual incompatibility or resistance to integration, (3) the resulting strain or tension that marks the state as perceptible. Persistence: the concept lives in acoustic theory, cognitive psychology, and general systems discourse — maintained through terminology, teaching, and the continued application of the incompatibility criterion across domains. [formal: dissonantia | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A parable is a brief, concrete narrative constructed to convey an abstract moral or spiritual lesson through analogy. Its parameters: (1) a simplified story with identifiable characters and a clear situation, (2) a mapping between narrative elements and the intended lesson, (3) an explicit or near-explicit moral principle that the listener or reader is meant to extract. The parable persists through intentional teaching — passed down in religious instruction, educational settings, and cultural tradition. It is distinct from fable (which features animals and a stated moral) and parable's domain is the ethical and spiritual instruction. [formal: parabola | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

Vocalization is a human-made concept designating the category of sounds produced by modulating air through the larynx and articulatory organs — a map for classifying what the body produces when breath is shaped by structured anatomy. Its parameters: (1) an air source driven by respiration, (2) phonation via vocal fold vibration (voiced) or turbulent narrowing (unvoiced), (3) articulation through the tract — lips, teeth, tongue, palate — that sculps raw sound into distinguishable units. It persists through linguistic teaching, anatomical study, and the cultural practices of singing, speech, and vocal performance. The map boundaries vary by discipline: phonetics isolates physical acoustics, linguistics isolates functional phonemes, music isolates pitch-contour, and medicine isolates pathology. [formal: vocalisatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A fastener is a human-made concept designating the category of mechanical devices engineered to join or secure two or more objects together. Its parameters: (1) a physical component or system that creates a non-permanent or semi-permanent connection, (2) a specified class of forms (bolts, screws, rivets, clips, ties) defined by their engagement mechanism rather than by material, (3) a functional boundary distinguishing joining from welding or adhesive bonding — fasteners enable disassembly. The persistence mechanism is standardization through engineering specifications, trade catalogs, and educational curricula that transmit the concept across technical practice. [formal: alligatio | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An oscillation is a human-made concept designating the category of phenomena in which a quantity varies periodically around a central equilibrium value. Its parameters: (1) a measurable state that returns repeatedly to a reference point, (2) a characteristic frequency or period governing the repetition rate, (3) a distinction between free oscillation (self-sustained, e.g. pendulum) and driven oscillation (externally forced, e.g. alternating current). The persistence mechanism is mathematical formalism through differential equations, engineering standards, and pedagogical transmission across the physical sciences. [formal: oscilatio | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

An echo is a human-made concept designating the category of reflected sound waves that return to a listener with sufficient delay to be perceived as distinct from the original. Its parameters: (1) a sound wave reflected from a surface or boundary, (2) a propagation delay long enough for perceptual separation from the source, (3) sufficient amplitude to be audible above ambient noise. Persistence through acoustical modeling, architectural design, musical composition, and linguistic categorization. [formal: echo | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Memento mori is a human-made concept designating the deliberate practice of contemplating one's own mortality. Its parameters: (1) an intentional act of reflection on the finitude of life, (2) performed not for despair but for clarification of values and priorities, (3) instantiated across cultures through artifacts (skulls, hourglasses, vanitas paintings), literary forms, and philosophical schools. The practice persists through cultural transmission — taught in philosophical traditions (Stoicism, Buddhism), embedded in artistic memento mori symbols, ritualized in memorial observances, and adopted in modern therapeutic and reflective practices. It is a map of finitude, not finitude itself. [formal: memento mori | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

A wave is a human-made concept designating the mathematical model of a propagating disturbance that transfers energy through a medium or vacuum without net transport of matter. Its parameters: (1) a disturbance from equilibrium state, (2) propagation at finite speed governed by the medium's properties, (3) energy or information transport without bulk matter transport. Waves manifest as mechanical (sound, seismic), electromagnetic (light, radio), or quantum (matter waves). Persistence through mathematical formalism (differential equations, Fourier analysis) and experimental measurement. [formal: wave | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Symmetry is a human-made concept designating invariance under transformation — the property that a configuration, object, system, or relationship retains specified attributes when a transformation is applied. Its parameters: (1) a domain (geometric, algebraic, physical, perceptual), (2) a transformation group acting on that domain, (3) the subset of transformations that leave the object or property unchanged (the symmetry group or symmetry subgroup). The concept carves four principal senses: geometric symmetry (reflection, rotation, translation), algebraic symmetry (commutativity, invariance of equations), physical symmetry (conservation laws via Noether's theorem), and perceptual symmetry (balanced visual or structural composition). It persists through mathematical formalism, scientific classification, artistic theory, and everyday descriptive language. [formal: symmetrica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A beat is a regularly recurring pulse of emphasis in time, the temporal unit that organizes rhythmic experience in music, poetry, and movement. It is the measured interval between successive accents that structures temporal perception into patterned units — the metronomic backbone of musical meter and the stress alternations that govern prosodic rhythm in verse. A beat does not require sound: it operates as an abstract temporal scaffold that can be realized through sound, gesture, speech, or even imagined internally, but its persistence mechanism is the human capacity to track regular intervals and to coordinate action to them. The beat is the map of temporal regularity that humans impose on flowing time, enabling synchronization across bodies and between body and artifact.[formal: pulsus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Tension is the state of strain produced by opposing forces, influences, or demands. It exists across domains — material, musical, psychological, social — wherever two or more tendencies pull against each other, creating a condition that seeks relief. Tension is not the forces themselves but the relationship between them: the gap between equilibrium and the current state. It is measurable (stress in pascals, pitch deviation in hertz, psychological scales) and felt (discomfort, anticipation, urgency). Tension persists until resolved, redistributed, or accepted as a steady state. [formal: tensionem | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Pressure is the intensity of force applied per unit of area, extent, or scope. It measures how concentrated the push is — whether that push is physical (fluid molecules colliding with a surface), social (collective expectation on an individual), or psychological (internal demand exceeding capacity). Pressure always points toward change: it seeks to compress, displace, or transform whatever resists it. Where tension is the state of strain from opposing forces, pressure is the active concentration of force seeking release. [formal: pressio | substrate: matter | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Consonance is the state of harmonious combination where simultaneous sounds or elements blend without acoustic or perceptual clash. It exists as a qualitative judgment made by listeners — trained or untrained — that certain combinations of frequencies produce a stable, unified percept rather than friction or beating. Parameters: (1) acoustic: intervals with simple frequency ratios (octave 2:1, fifth 3:2, fourth 4:3) are most consonant; (2) contextual: consonance varies across musical cultures and historical periods; (3) perceptual: it is experienced as stability and rest, the counterpart to dissonance's instability. Persistence: the concept persists through music-theoretic teaching, acoustic analysis frameworks, and cross-cultural aesthetic categorization. [formal: consonantia | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: no | epoch: 0.01]

A simulacrum is a representation that has no original — a copy without a model, or a representation that has replaced and concealed the absence of an original. It is not merely a false copy but a generation of the real by a model: the simulacrum produces reality through its own internal logic of signs. Three orders distinguish it: (1) a faithful copy bearing the secret corruption of an underlying reality, (2) a copy that masks and perverts an ordinary reality, and (3) a copy that bears no relation to any reality whatsoever — it is its own pure simulacrum. The simulacrum persists through philosophical discourse, semiotic analysis, and cultural critique as a tool for diagnosing the displacement of reality by its representations. [formal: simulacrum | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An overtone is any frequency component of a complex sound that exceeds the fundamental frequency. Parameters: (1) it must be a component of a harmonic or inharmonic complex tone; (2) its frequency is strictly above the fundamental. Persistence: the concept persists through musical acoustics, spectral analysis methodology, and instrument design practice — encoded in the overtone series table, used in timbre classification, and applied in sound synthesis and tuning system design. The overtone map distinguishes harmonic overtones (integer multiples of the fundamental) from inharmonic overtones (non-integer multiples), a distinction humans made to organize acoustic phenomena. [formal: superonus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A harmonic series is the ordered sequence of frequencies f_n = n × f_0 where f_0 is a fundamental frequency and n ranges over positive integers (1, 2, 3, ...). Parameters: (1) each member is an exact integer multiple of the fundamental; (2) the sequence is ordered by increasing frequency; (3) the first member (n=1) IS the fundamental itself. The harmonic series persists as a concept through spectral analysis, musical acoustics, and tuning theory — it is used to model the physical structure of complex tones, explain overtone content, and justify just-intonation tuning systems. [formal: seria-harmonica | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A spectrum is an analytical representation that maps a measured or computed quantity (amplitude, power, intensity) to a domain variable (frequency, wavelength, energy, mass). Parameters: (1) the domain axis, which determines the type of spectrum (e.g. frequency spectrum, mass spectrum); (2) the magnitude axis, representing the strength of the quantity at each domain point; (3) resolution, which determines the finest distinguishable separation in the domain. A spectrum persists through mathematical formalism (Fourier transforms, spectral decomposition), instrumental output (spectrograms, spectrum analyzers), and notational conventions (plots, color maps). It is the primary tool for decomposing complex signals into constituent components — the bridge between raw measurement and structural understanding. [formal: spectrum | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Equilibrium is a state in which competing forces, influences, or tendencies are balanced such that no net change occurs. It has two forms: static equilibrium (forces cancel completely, producing rest) and dynamic equilibrium (opposing flows maintain a steady state). The concept persists through mathematical modeling — solving for zero net force or steady-state flow — and empirical verification across disciplines including physics, chemistry, economics, and psychology. The parameters are: (1) identification of competing vectors, (2) calculation of their net effect, (3) determination of whether the net effect is zero or balanced. The persistence mechanism is the repeated application of this model to predict and stabilize systems.

Pitch is the perceptual attribute of sound that allows auditory experiences to be ordered on a frequency-related scale from low to high. Parameters: (1) the physical stimulus is a periodic sound wave characterized by a fundamental frequency measured in Hertz; (2) the perceptual mapping from frequency to pitch is approximately logarithmic — equal multiplicative ratios in frequency produce equal additive steps in pitch (the basis for musical intervals and octaves); (3) pitch is not purely determined by frequency — timbre, intensity, and duration modulate pitch perception, especially at frequency extremes where the ear's non-linear response distorts the mapping. Persistence mechanism: pitch is encoded in musical notation systems (staff notation, tab), institutionalized in tuning standards (A440, equal temperament), embedded in instrument design (fret spacing, organ pipe length), and transmitted through pedagogy and cultural practice across generations. [formal: pitch | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Polyphony is the compositional practice of combining two or more independent melodic voices into a single simultaneous texture. Parameters: (1) the minimum number of voices is two (dyadic polyphony); (2) each voice maintains melodically independent contour and rhythmic identity; (3) voices are structured to be perceptible as distinct lines within the composite. Persistence mechanism: maintained through notation systems, pedagogical tradition, and compositional practice passed across generations. [formal: polyphonia | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Frequency is the count of recurring events per unit of time, expressed as cycles, oscillations, or vibrations per second (hertz). It quantifies periodicity by measuring how often a repeating pattern completes in a given interval. Parameters: measurable rate of cyclic recurrence, applicable to waves, rotations, oscillations, and any temporally repeated phenomenon. Persists through mathematical formalization in physics, engineering notation, and musical pitch classification. [formal: freqüentia | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Melody is a sequence of pitched notes arranged in time to form a coherent musical unit. Its parameters are: (1) pitch succession — notes ordered by frequency, (2) temporal organization — notes arranged in a specific rhythm and duration, (3) contour — the overall shape of pitch movement (ascending, descending, undulating), and (4) recognizability — the pattern must be distinguishable as a single identity from the surrounding music. It persists through performance (sound waves carrying structured pitch sequences), notation (written representation of pitch and duration), and memory (cognitive retention of the pattern). [formal: melodia | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Flow is a psychological state of deep, focused engagement in an activity, characterized by five operational parameters: (1) intense concentration on the present moment — attention narrows to activity-relevant stimuli, (2) merging of action and awareness — doing feels automatic, without deliberate monitoring, (3) loss of reflective self-consciousness — the evaluating self recedes, (4) sense of personal control or agency over the activity, and (5) transformation of temporal experience — time feels contracted or expanded relative to clock time. Its persistence mechanism is empirical: established through systematic psychological research, validated across domains (sports, music, coding, art), codified in peer-reviewed literature and applied frameworks in coaching and education. The construct endures because it names a reproducible quality of human attention that interventions can reliably elicit and measure. [formal: fluxus | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.91]

Tuning is the practice of establishing and maintaining standardized pitch relationships within a musical system. Its parameters are: (1) reference pitch — a fixed frequency assigned to a named note (e.g. A4=440 Hz), (2) temperament — the system of interval sizes (equal, just, meantone) that determines which frequencies are accepted, (3) calibration procedure — the technique by which instruments are adjusted to the chosen standard. Tuning persists through institutional standardization (ISO concert pitch), pedagogical transmission, and the material tolerances of instrument manufacture. [formal: tuning | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Interval is a human-made musical concept that names, measures, and classifies the distance between two pitches within a given tuning system. Its parameters are: (1) step count — the number of scale degrees separating the two notes; (2) quality classification — perfect, major, minor, augmented, or diminished; (3) size in cents — a logarithmic measure of frequency ratio that enables precise comparison across tuning systems. The interval functions as both an analytical label and a perceptual category, allowing musicians and theorists to reference, compare, and reason about pitch relationships independently of any specific instrument or frequency. [formal: intervallum | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A waveform is the mapping of a signal's amplitude (or other varying quantity) onto a temporal axis, producing a shape that encodes the signal's morphological properties. Its parameters are: the dependent variable (amplitude, pressure, voltage), the independent variable (time or spatial position), and the functional form (continuous or discrete). Waveforms persist through four mechanisms: (1) visual notation on paper or screen (oscillograms, spectrograms), (2) digital representation (sampled arrays in digital audio, vector graphics), (3) mathematical description (parametric functions like A·sin(2πft+φ)), and (4) physical transduction (needle grooves on vinyl, ink on paper chart recorders). The waveform distinguishes signal morphology from signal content — two signals with identical waveforms carry the same morphological information regardless of their physical carrier. Waveforms are classified by shape: sine (single frequency), square (abrupt transitions), sawtooth (linear ramp), triangle (symmetric ramp), pulse (brief impulse), and noise (stochastic). This classification is a human-made taxonomy; the natural world contains only electromagnetic or mechanical phenomena, not waveforms. [formal: waveform | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Harmonics are the integer-multiple frequencies produced by a vibrating system alongside its fundamental. Parameters: the fundamental frequency f₀, the harmonic series (n·f₀ for n=1,2,3,...), and the amplitude envelope across partials. Persistence: sustained through mathematical notation, acoustic measurement apparatus, and pedagogical teaching of instrument acoustics. [formal: harmonica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

A formant is a resonant frequency band of the vocal tract — a peak in spectral energy produced when the vocal tract acts as an acoustic filter, amplifying harmonics at specific frequencies. Formants are determined by the shape and size of the vocal tract cavity and are the primary acoustic cue for distinguishing vowel sounds. Measured through spectral analysis (FFT, LPC) and expressed in Hertz. [formal: formantum | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Loudness is the perceptual correlate of acoustic stimulus intensity — the subjective magnitude with which a listener experiences sound pressure. It is not identical to sound pressure level (SPL); rather, loudness is the mind's mapping of physical amplitude onto a psychological scale, governed by Stevens' power law (perceived magnitude ≈ k × stimulus^n, where n≈0.6 for loudness). Damping is the concept of controlled energy dissipation in an oscillating system — the introduction of a resistive force proportional to velocity that reduces amplitude over time. Transient is the concept of a brief, short-duration phenomenon — specifically in acoustics and audio processing, it names the initial attack phase of a sound characterized by rapid amplitude rise and high energy concentration before the steady-state or sustain phase. Defined by its temporal parameters (typically 1–50ms duration) and its spectral content (rich in harmonics due to the abrupt onset). The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is an algorithm that computes the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) of a sequence, or its inverse (IDFT). It transforms a finite sequence of equally-spaced samples of a function from its time-domain representation to its frequency-domain representation. The algorithm exploits symmetries in the DFT computation to reduce complexity from O(n²) to O(n log n). The parameters defining it are: (1) input: N complex numbers representing time-domain samples, (2) output: N complex numbers representing frequency-domain coefficients, (3) method: recursive decomposition of the DFT matrix using butterfly operations. It persists through implementation as a standardized algorithm in numerical computing libraries (NumPy, FFTW, Intel MKT) and hardware instructions. [formal: fft | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) is a mathematical transformation that maps a finite sequence of N time-domain samples x[0], ..., x[N-1] to a finite sequence of N complex frequency-domain coefficients X[0], ..., X[N-1], computed by the formula X[k] = Σ(n=0 to N-1) x[n] · e^(-2πi·k·n/N) for k = 0, ..., N-1. The transform decomposes a signal into its constituent sinusoidal frequencies, enabling spectral analysis, filtering, and convolution. It persists as a defined algorithm in numerical libraries (NumPy, FFTW), a standard operation in DSP toolchains, and a foundational concept in engineering education. The inverse DFT reconstructs the time-domain signal from the frequency coefficients. [formal: dft | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

Phase is the human-made concept of a point within the cycle of a periodic waveform, quantified as an angle (radians or degrees) or fraction of a complete period. The concept operates across signal processing, acoustics, electrical engineering, and wave mechanics as the standard measure of cyclic position. The attack is the initial phase of a sound's amplitude envelope — the time interval and trajectory from silence to peak amplitude when a sound begins. [formal: atacatus | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The impulse-response is the complete characterization of a linear time-invariant (LTI) system given by its output when the input is a Dirac delta function — an idealized infinitesimally-brief unit pulse. The impulse-response persists as a conceptual framework in engineering mathematics, deployed across signal processing, control theory, acoustics, and communications to analyze, design, and predict system behavior. The amplitude-envelope is a formal model of how the magnitude (amplitude/loudness) of a sound or signal evolves over time. A convolution is a mathematical operation that combines two functions to produce a third, expressing how the shape of one is modified by the other. A phasor is a human-made representational construct in electrical engineering and signal processing that encodes a sinusoidal steady-state signal as a single complex number, capturing amplitude and phase while suppressing the implicit carrier frequency and time dependence. Overshoot is a quantifiable metric in signal processing and control theory that measures the maximum percentage by which a system's step response exceeds its final steady-state value before settling. Impedance is the complex-valued measure of opposition that a circuit element or network presents to sinusoidal current at a given frequency. Parameters: (1) the group-delay function τ_g(ω) = -dφ/dω, where φ is the phase response and ω is angular frequency; (2) positive group-delay indicates delay, negative indicates phase advancement; (3) constant group-delay across frequencies preserves signal shape, while frequency-dependent group-delay causes distortion. Windowing is a human-made technique in signal processing that multiplies a signal segment by a mathematical window function to reduce spectral leakage during Fourier analysis. Parameters: (1) window shape (Hann, Hamming, Blackman, Kaiser, or custom) determining the trade-off between main-lobe width and side-lobe suppression, (2) window length matching the analysis segment, (3) application mode (rectangular, overlapping with overlap-add or overlap-save). [formal: windowing | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 2.50]

Reactance is the imaginary component (X) of complex impedance in AC circuit analysis, quantifying opposition to sinusoidal current arising from energy storage rather than resistive dissipation. Parameters: (1) inductive reactance X_L = ωL (positive, from inductors storing energy in magnetic fields); (2) capacitive reactance X_C = -1/(ωC) (negative, from capacitors storing energy in electric fields). Ringing is the concept of sustained oscillations that persist in a dynamic system's output after a transient disturbance has ended. The persistence mechanism is the mathematical model of underdamped second-order systems (differential equations with complex conjugate poles) and empirical observation in physical systems including electrical circuits, mechanical structures, and acoustic resonators. The sinc function is the mathematical function sinc(x) = sin(πx)/(πx), defined piecewise with sinc(0) = 1 by continuity. It is a cornerstone of Fourier analysis, appearing as the Fourier transform of the rectangular window and as the impulse response of an ideal low-pass filter. Its zeros at integer values (x ≠ 0) enable exact signal reconstruction through interpolation. [formal: sinc | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

Spectral leakage is the artificial spreading of signal energy across frequency bins in a discrete Fourier transform, caused by the finite observation window effectively multiplying the signal by a rectangular window. Because multiplication in time equals convolution in frequency, the true spectrum becomes convolved with the window's transform (a sinc function), causing energy from a single frequency to 'leak' into adjacent bins. The phenomenon is governed by the window length, the signal's frequency resolution relative to the bin spacing, and the choice of window function used to mitigate it. Parameters: observation window length N, bin spacing Fs/N, window shape (rectangular, Hamming, Hann, etc.). Persists through the mathematical formalism of Fourier analysis and the practical conventions of signal processing instrumentation. [formal: leakage spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Aliasing is the error artifact that occurs when a continuous signal is sampled at a rate below twice its highest frequency component (the Nyquist criterion), causing frequency components above the Nyquist limit to fold back and appear as spurious lower-frequency signals. The phenomenon is parameterized by the undersampling ratio (fsignalfsnysquig), the amplitude of aliased components (determined by the spectral content above fs/2 and the anti-aliasing filter roll-off), and the alias frequency (falias = |finput - n·fsampler| for integer n). Aliasing persists through engineering practice: it is modeled in ADC datasheets, prevented by anti-aliasing filters in signal chains, and managed in software via oversampling and decimation. The concept is taught in every signal processing curriculum and enforced in hardware design specifications.\n\n[formal: aliasing | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The Nyquist criterion is a theorem in signal processing that establishes the minimum sampling rate required for perfect reconstruction of a continuous-time signal. It states that the sampling rate fs must satisfy fs > 2·fmax, where fmax is the highest frequency present in the signal. The value 2·fmax is the Nyquist rate. Below this rate, frequency components above fs/2 fold back (alias) into the baseband, making perfect reconstruction impossible. The criterion persists through formal proof in sampling theory and is enforced in all digital signal processing systems. [formal: criterium-samplingis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

A window function is a mathematical function that assigns a smoothly decaying weighting to the samples of a finite data segment, effectively tapering the signal amplitude toward zero at the boundaries. It is applied before a Fourier transform to minimize spectral leakage caused by the implicit rectangular window of finite observation. The class includes the Hamming, Hanning, Blackman, and Kaiser windows, each optimizing different tradeoffs between main-lobe width and side-lobe attenuation. Persistence mechanism: mathematical formulas codified in signal-processing literature and implemented in DSP toolkits. [formal: functio clavi | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.42]

Zero-padding is a signal-processing technique in which zeros are appended to a finite discrete-time signal before computing its Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT). The operation does not add information to the signal but interpolates the spectral estimate by increasing the number of frequency bins, yielding a smoother spectrum that better reveals peak locations and spectral detail. The persistence mechanism is digital signal processing practice: the technique is embedded in every DFT implementation and taught as standard procedure in signal analysis. [formal: padding-matematica | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An anti-aliasing filter is a low-pass signal-processing circuit or algorithm applied before the sampling stage of an analog-to-digital conversion. It attenuates frequency components above the Nyquist frequency (half the sampling rate) to prevent higher-frequency signals from folding back into the baseband as aliasing artifacts. Its design specifies a cutoff frequency at or below the Nyquist limit and a roll-off steepness sufficient to suppress out-of-band content to below the quantization noise floor. It persists through electronic hardware (RC networks, active filter topologies, SAW devices) and software implementations (digital filter coefficients for pre-sampling preprocessing). [formal: anti-aliasing-filter | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

Frequency resolution is the minimum frequency separation at which two sinusoidal components can be distinguished as separate peaks in a spectral estimate. For the DFT with N samples at sampling rate fs, the bin spacing is fs/N; effective resolution is worsened by window function main-lobe width. Formally: the resolution limit is the smallest Δf such that two spectral components at f and f+Δf produce distinguishable peaks. [formal: discretaspectus | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral density quantifies how signal power or energy is distributed across frequency. For deterministic signals, the energy spectral density is the squared magnitude of the Fourier transform; for stochastic processes, the power spectral density is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation function (Wiener–Khinchin theorem). Measured in watts per hertz (W/Hz). Units and normalization depend on convention (one-sided vs. two-sided, periodogram vs. Welch's method). [formal: densitasspectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Power spectrum quantifies the distribution of signal power across frequency, showing which frequency bands carry the most energy. For deterministic energy signals, it is computed as the squared magnitude of the Fourier transform |X(f)|²; for stochastic power signals, it is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation function via the Wiener-Khinchin theorem. The power spectrum persists as a core analytical construct in signal processing, communications, and spectral analysis, where it enables engineers to diagnose system behavior, design filters, and characterize noise. [formal: spectrum potentiae | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Transient response is the time-domain behavior of a system following a sudden change (step, impulse, or pulse) in its input. It comprises three phases: initial reaction (rise time and overshoot), oscillatory behavior (ringing at the system's natural or resonant frequencies), and settling to the final steady-state value. The transient response is characterized by parameters including rise time, peak time, maximum overshoot, settling time, and decay ratio. It is fundamental to control theory, signal processing, and circuit design where rapid and stable system behavior is required. The transient response is determined by the system's poles in the complex plane — underdamped poles produce oscillatory transients, overdamped poles produce smooth exponential approaches, and critically damped poles produce the fastest non-oscillatory response.\n\n[formal: transient response | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

The Fourier transform is a human-made mathematical framework that maps a function (typically a signal in time domain) into a representation in terms of its constituent frequencies. It operates by applying an integral kernel e^(-jωt) to decompose functions into sinusoidal components, yielding a complex-valued frequency-domain function. The inverse transform reconstructs the original function from its spectral components. The framework persists through formal mathematical notation, algorithmic implementations (including the Fast Fourier Transform), and pedagogical tradition across mathematics, physics, and engineering. It establishes a duality between time-domain and frequency-domain descriptions of the same phenomenon, enabling analysis that is intractable in the original domain. [formal: fourier-transform | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The hamming window is a human-made mathematical function used in signal processing to taper signals before spectral analysis. It is defined by the formula w(n) = 0.54 - 0.46*cos(2*pi*n/(N-1)) for n in [0, N-1], where N is the window length. Its parameters are the amplitude coefficients (0.54, 0.46) and the window length N. It persists as a standardized construct in signal processing literature, software libraries, and engineering practice. [formal: hamming | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The spectral analysis is a human-made practice for decomposing a signal into its constituent frequency components and examining how energy, amplitude, and phase are distributed across those frequencies. It operates by applying a mathematical transform — most commonly the Fourier transform, but also wavelet transforms, short-time Fourier transforms, or cosine transforms — to a time-domain or spatial-domain representation of a signal, producing a frequency-domain description from which features such as dominant frequencies, spectral density, harmonic content, and spectral leakage can be extracted. The practice persists through standardized algorithms implemented in signal-processing software and hardware, taught as a core technique in engineering, physics, and applied mathematics, and institutionalized in standards bodies that specify measurement procedures and analysis windows. [formal: spectri analasis | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The ringdown is a human-made concept describing the gradual decay of oscillatory motion in a physical or engineered system after the excitation force is removed. [formal: ringdown | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The linearity is a human-made concept describing a class of systems whose behavior satisfies two properties: homogeneity (scaling the input scales the output by the same factor) and superposition (the response to a sum of inputs equals the sum of individual responses). Linearity is the foundational property that enables powerful analytical tools in engineering and physics, including Fourier analysis, Laplace transforms, and convolution-based system characterization. It persists through mathematical formalism, engineering practice, and computational simulation. [formal: linearitas | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The phase response is a human-made concept in signal processing that specifies how different frequency components of a signal are shifted in phase by a linear system. It is the angular component of the complex frequency response H(ω) = |H(ω)|·e^(jφ(ω)), where φ(ω) denotes the phase shift at each frequency. Key parameters include linear phase (constant group delay, preserving waveform shape) and nonlinear phase (introducing dispersion and phase distortion). It persists as a mathematical descriptor used in filter design, audio engineering, and communication theory. [formal: responsio phaenomeni | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

It carves the transform as a generalization of the Fourier transform by allowing a complex frequency variable, enabling analysis of signals and systems that are not absolutely integrable. Its persistence mechanism is mathematical formalism: defined through integral tables, operational calculus, and taught as a standard tool in engineering and physics curricula. [formal: laplace-transformatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral-resolution is the human-made parameter that quantifies the minimum frequency separation required to distinguish two distinct spectral components as separate peaks in a frequency-domain representation of a signal. It is determined by the analysis method's parameters — for a Fourier transform, resolution is inversely proportional to the observation window duration (Δf ≈ 1/T) — and by the window function's main-lobe width. A definition must specify: (1) the analysis method (DFT, filter bank, parametric model), (2) the observable (amplitude peaks, phase coherence, energy concentration), and (3) the threshold for distinguishability (Rayleigh criterion, -3 dB separation, signal-to-noise ratio). Spectral-resolution persists through instrument datasheets, measurement standards (IEEE), engineering textbooks, and the mathematical theory of spectral estimation. [formal: resolutio spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral leakage is the human-made phenomenon where the finite observation of a signal causes its frequency spectrum to spread beyond the true frequency components, producing artificial side-lobes. It is mitigated by non-rectangular window functions that reduce side-lobe amplitude at the cost of main-lobe width. [formal: fuga spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A cepstrum is a signal processing transform that maps a power spectrum into a quefrency domain by applying the inverse Fourier transform to the logarithm of the power spectrum. The procedure: (1) compute the power spectrum of a signal via FFT, (2) take the natural logarithm of each spectral magnitude, (3) apply the inverse FFT to the log-spectrum. The resulting quefrency-axis representation separates slowly-varying spectral envelopes (filter) from rapidly-varying fine structure (source), enabling tasks like pitch detection in speech, rolling-centre removal in spectroscopy, and fault diagnosis in mechanical vibrations. The transform was named by reversing 'spectrum' to 'quefrency' to distinguish it from frequency while preserving the formal analogy. [formal: cepstrum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Deconvolution is a signal processing technique that recovers an estimate of an original source signal from an observed signal degraded by convolution with a known kernel. Given an observed signal y = x * h (where * denotes convolution and h is the known point-spread function), deconvolution computes an estimate of x through methods including inverse filtering, Wiener deconvolution, and iterative algorithms such as the Richardson-Lucy method. The procedure operates in either the frequency domain (dividing the observed spectrum by the kernel's transfer function) or the time domain (applying deconvolution filters or optimization). Deconvolution underpins applications in spectroscopy, microscopy, communications, and audio restoration. [formal: deconvolutio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A spectrogram is a visual display that maps signal energy across frequency and time, produced by computing successive short-time Fourier transforms with a defined window size and overlap, then rendering the resulting magnitude spectrum as a color- or intensity-coded image. Its parameters are: the input signal, window function (e.g. Hann, Hamming), window length, and hop size. It persists as a rendered image or data plot generated by signal processing software and stored in display media. [formal: spectrogram | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is a signal-processing procedure that partitions a signal into short, overlapping time windows using a window function (e.g., Hann, Hamming, or Gaussian), computes the discrete Fourier transform of each windowed segment, and stacks the results into a time-localized frequency representation. The method carves the signal into a two-dimensional time–frequency matrix whose resolution is governed by the window width: narrower windows trade frequency resolution for temporal precision, while wider windows do the reverse. The persistence mechanism is algorithmic — the computation is defined by the sequence of windowing, Fourier transformation, and assembly, implementable in software or hardware. [formal: stft | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A cepstral coefficient is a single value in the cepstrum sequence, representing one spectral envelope feature extracted from the logarithm of a power spectrum. Cepstral coefficients are computed by: (1) computing the power spectral density of a signal, (2) taking the natural logarithm of the spectrum, (3) applying the inverse Fourier transform to obtain the cepstrum, and (4) selecting individual coefficients from the resulting sequence. The first few coefficients encode the spectral envelope shape, while higher-order coefficients encode fine spectral details. In speech processing, the Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) use a Mel-scale filterbank in step 1 to mimic human auditory perception. The number of coefficients retained is a design parameter, typically 12–24 for speech applications. The persistence mechanism is algorithmic: coefficients are computed on demand by the cepstral analysis procedure and stored as numerical arrays in digital signal processing systems.[formal: coefficientes-cepstrales | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.15]

Quefrency is a human-made variable introduced with cepstral analysis to name the independent axis of the cepstrum — it measures periodicity in a frequency spectrum, expressed as a 'reverse time' whose units match those of the original domain (e.g., milliseconds). It is not a physical time but a computational abstraction: the value on the quefrency axis at which the cepstrum peaks indicates the spacing (in the original domain) between spectral harmonics or resonances. The cepstrum was invented by Bogert, Healy, and Tukey (1963); the term quefrency is a portmanteau of 'spectrum' and 'frequency' (suffix -queincy echoing -ency) to signal that it is the dual-domain counterpart of time in Fourier analysis, with the name chosen so that 'time' in quefrency reads back as 'frequency' in the original domain. [formal: quefrency | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The spectral centroid is a human-made measure used in signal and audio processing that quantifies the 'center of mass' of a spectrum's magnitude distribution — the point at which the energy of the spectrum would balance if it were a physical object. It is computed as the weighted mean of the frequency components, where the weights are the magnitudes at each frequency, and is typically expressed in Hertz. The spectral centroid serves as a proxy for the perceptual attribute of 'brightness' in sound, since higher centroids correspond to more high-frequency energy. It is a scalar descriptor extracted from a single spectrum frame and is widely used in audio analysis, instrument recognition, and music information retrieval. [formal: spectral-centroid | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A time-frequency representation (TFR) is a signal-processing technique that maps a one-dimensional time-domain signal into a two-dimensional representation showing how frequency content varies over time. Unlike the Fourier transform, which collapses all temporal information into a static spectrum, a TFR preserves the joint time-frequency structure of non-stationary signals. Common families include linear TFRs such as the spectrogram (short-time Fourier transform with a window function) and the Wigner-Ville distribution (a quadratic formulation offering superior resolution at the cost of cross-term interference). The parameter space consists of time center, frequency bandwidth, and window shape; the persistence mechanism is mathematical transformation applied to signal data. A TFR enables the analysis of transient features, frequency modulation, and time-varying spectral content that would be invisible in a plain Fourier spectrum. [formal: temporis-frequentialis-repraesentatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The phase spectrum of a signal is the function that assigns, to each frequency component in a spectral decomposition, the phase angle (argument) of the corresponding complex-valued spectral coefficient. It is obtained by applying a frequency-domain transform (Fourier, Laplace, or Z-transform) and extracting the argument of the resulting complex output — complementing the magnitude spectrum, which records the amplitude of each component. The phase spectrum encodes the timing and alignment relationships among frequency components; it determines how those components superpose to reconstruct the original signal's waveform. Without the phase spectrum, the magnitude spectrum alone cannot recover the signal's temporal structure. The concept persists as a theoretical construct in signal analysis, system identification, and audio processing, where phase information is essential for tasks such as phase retrieval, group-delay analysis, and coherent signal reconstruction. [formal: spectrum phase | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The magnitude spectrum of a signal is the function mapping each frequency to the amplitude (modulus) of the corresponding complex-valued spectral coefficient from a frequency-domain transform (Fourier, Laplace, or Z-transform). It records the energy distribution of the signal across frequencies — which frequency components are strong and which are weak — but alone cannot reconstruct the original signal's waveform, since the phase angles of each component are also required. Computationally, it is obtained as |X(f)| = sqrt(Re(X(f))^2 + Im(X(f))^2) where X(f) is the complex spectrum. The magnitude spectrum persists as a fundamental analytical tool in signal processing, spectroscopy, acoustic analysis, and communications, where power spectral density estimation and frequency-domain characterization depend on it. [formal: spectrum magnitude | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Cepstral analysis is the signal processing technique that transforms a signal's spectral representation into the quefrency domain by computing the inverse Fourier transform of the logarithm of the magnitude spectrum. The method operates on the principle that convolution in the time domain becomes addition in the spectral domain, and taking the logarithm converts convolved components into additive ones; the inverse Fourier transform then separates these additive components into distinct quefrency regions where periodic spectral structures manifest as peaks. The technique carves its parameters as follows: input is a magnitude spectrum, the transformation sequence is (1) take the natural logarithm, (2) apply inverse Fourier transform, (3) extract quefrency-domain representation; output is a cepstrum — a signal in quefrency where peaks indicate repeating spectral patterns such as harmonic structures or echo delays. Persistence is achieved through mathematical formalism documented in signal processing literature since Bogert, Healy, and Tukey (1963). [formal: analisis cepstral | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Arithmetic is the branch of mathematics concerned with the operations on numbers and the study of properties of certain algebraic structures arising from addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. It operates through formal rules governing numerical computation, persisting through written notation, algorithmic procedures, and institutionalized teaching across human cultures. [formal: arithmetica | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) is a mathematical algorithm that converts a finite sequence of N time-domain samples into a finite sequence of N frequency-domain complex coefficients. It computes X[k] = sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] * exp(-2*pi*i*k*n/N) for k = 0,...,N-1, thereby decomposing a discrete signal into its constituent frequencies. The DFT is the foundational transform of digital signal processing, enabling spectral analysis, filtering, and convolution in the digital domain. [formal: DFT | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is a dimensionless quantitative measure that compares the power level of a desired signal to the power level of background noise. It is defined as SNR = P_signal / P_noise, where P denotes average power. In decibels: SNR(dB) = 10·log₁₀(P_signal / P_noise). The parameter that defines SNR is the signal and noise power measurements taken over a defined bandwidth. It persists through mathematical formulas, engineering specifications, instrument readouts, and standardized measurement protocols across communications, audio engineering, imaging, and scientific measurement. [formal: signal-to-noise-ratio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.83]

Signal-processing is the human-made discipline of analyzing, modifying, and synthesizing signals — mathematical representations of information carried by measurable quantities — to extract meaning, compress data, detect patterns, or produce desired outputs. It operates by applying mathematical transforms (Fourier, wavelet, cepstral), filtering operations, and computational algorithms to signals in domains such as time, frequency, or quefrency. Its persistence mechanism is the body of algorithms, software implementations, and theoretical frameworks taught across engineering and applied mathematics disciplines. [formal: processingus | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A cepstrum-coefficient is the individual amplitude value obtained at a specific quefrency from the cepstrum computation: the inverse Fourier transform of the logarithm of a signal's power spectrum. Each coefficient corresponds to one quefrency point and encodes periodic structure in the signal's spectrum — low quefrency coefficients capture broad spectral shape, high quefrency coefficients resolve fine spectral detail. The construct persists through standard notation (e.g., c[n] or Cep(n)), mathematical tables, and practical applications in speech recognition (MFCCs), fault diagnosis, and audio analysis. [formal: coefficient | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Statistical-analysis is the human-made methodological framework for collecting, examining, and interpreting data using mathematical-statistical techniques to extract meaning, discover patterns, and support inference. It operates through a defined pipeline: specifying a research question, designing data collection (sampling, measurement), applying descriptive statistics (summarizing data via measures of central tendency and dispersion), and deploying inferential techniques (hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, regression, Bayesian inference) to generalize from samples to populations. Its persistence mechanism is formalized in textbooks, software implementations (R, Python, SPSS), and institutionalized in scientific practice across every empirical discipline.
